content.text: The entire agreement is a single section, and I've read all 75 paragraphs. There is no non-solicitation, no-hire, or non-poaching provision anywhere.

input.quote: (c) The relationship of the Parties is that of independent contractors, and nothing herein is intended, nor should be construed, to create a partnership, agency, joint venture or employment relationship.
input.rationale: I read the full agreement (single "Preamble" section, paragraphs p0000–p0074) and searched for solicitation/hiring language; there is no non-solicitation, non-poaching or no-hire covenant anywhere. The General Provisions (p0063–p0073) cover governing law, publicity, independent contractor status, notices, severability/survival, force majeure and assignment, and the survival list in p0070 (confidentiality, proprietary rights, indemnification, limitations of liability, effects of termination, governing law) contains no restrictive covenant. Because no restriction is imposed on the Customer's ability to hire or approach Vendor personnel, the document sits at the playbook's preferred position ("No non-solicit on Customer"), so no redline is warranted. Note for the record: since the clause is simply absent, we should resist any attempt to introduce one on redraft, and if the Vendor insists we would only accept the fallback (mutual, limited to personnel directly involved in the Services, 12 months from the end of their involvement, with general-advertisement and unsolicited-approach carve-outs and no no-hire).
